plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do or believe, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks losses if you win at a price above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since values are private and independent, the optimal strategy is straightforward truth-telling: bid exactly my value of $25, ensuring maximum expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

In a second-price auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of beliefs about opponents' bidding behavior. Since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit in this format. My value is $17, so I will bid exactly that amount.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, truthful bidding is optimal here.
